framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Before releasing a generative AI system, the ministry's planners are to create input/output test scenarios based on its purpose and functions, test inputs and outputs, and confirm stable operation and expected quality. Illustrative methods: checking domain-prohibited outputs, inappropriate generation and social bias, conformity with procurement specifications, and diverse/independent internal and external testing such as red teaming.
what_is_tested: Input/output behaviour, stable operation, output quality, bias, prohibited outputs, specification conformity (red teaming as an example method)
who_tests: Planners in ministries/agencies; vendors/providers may verify data per contract; citizens may take part for public-facing systems
interpretation_note: Document positioned 'Normative' (rules to be adhered to for government information systems); binding on ministries as an administrative standard, not a statute. English provisional translation uses 'should'; Japanese original uses declarative 'jisshi suru' (carry out). Listed methods are examples. Meets the four-part test for required pre-deployment testing, for government bodies.
conflict_flag: EN provisional translation 'should' vs JA declarative form
language_read: English provisional translation (Digital Agency) checked against Japanese original

framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Each ministry's Chief AI Officer (CAIO), with planners, shall conduct use-case risk assessments and determine the risk level (including whether likely high-risk), referring to the High-Risk AI Project Finder (Appendix 1); likely high-risk cases are reported to the Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board; the CAIO makes the final determination.
what_is_tested: Use-case risk classification of generative AI (high-risk judgement)
who_tests: CAIO with planners; Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board advises
interpretation_note: Binding on ministries/agencies (normative government guideline). Risk assessment occurs at planning stage, before procurement and deployment.
language_read: English provisional translation (Digital Agency) checked against Japanese original

framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: CAIOs shall conduct risk assessments at project planning and, for generative AI systems likely to be high-risk, report project details, objectives, risk mitigation measures and quality assurance plans (including during operation) to the Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board; reporting also applies at development, release and post-launch if high-risk status arises; CAIOs report a status list about quarterly.
what_is_tested: Reporting of risk assessment, mitigation and quality assurance plans for likely high-risk generative AI
who_tests: CAIO reports to Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board
interpretation_note: Binding on ministries. Reporting/oversight enabler rather than a test itself.
language_read: English provisional translation (Digital Agency) checked against Japanese original

framework: South Korea - Enforcement Decree of the AI Framework Act (Presidential Decree No. 36053, 21 Jan 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: The impact assessment of high-impact AI must cover: affected persons/groups; affected fundamental rights; content and scope of social and economic impacts; usage patterns; quantitative and qualitative metrics and methods used; measures to prevent and mitigate risks and recover losses; and, where needed, an improvement plan. The operator may conduct it itself or commission a third party; the Minister notifies other matters.
what_is_tested: Fundamental rights impact assessment content and method
interpretation_note: translation: KLRI English, reference only. The decree sets content only; the underlying duty in Act Art. 35 is an 'endeavor' duty (coded voluntary in Korea-008, not re-read here). Timing ('in advance') comes from the Act, not the decree.
language_read: English translation by KLRI (site states English version is for reference only, no legal effect)

framework: South Korea - Enforcement Decree of the AI Framework Act (Presidential Decree No. 36053, 21 Jan 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: An operator requesting MSIT confirmation of whether its AI is high-impact files the Appendix form with a product/service overview, training data overview, materials verifying the AI's process and results, and other documents; MSIT decides on criteria including use area, impact/severity/frequency of risks to life, safety and rights, and the operator's prior review; response within 30 days (extendable once by 30 days); reconfirmation request within 10 days, answered within 30 days after consulting the specialised committee.
who_tests: Operator submits; MSIT decides with specialised committee
interpretation_note: translation: KLRI English, reference only. Triggered by the operator's request under Act Art. 33(2); complements Korea-006.
language_read: English translation by KLRI (site states English version is for reference only, no legal effect)

framework: China - TC260-PG-20268A Cybersecurity Standard Practice Guide: AI Application Security Guidelines, General (v1.0-202609, TC260 Secretariat, Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: In the verification and validation stage, organisations validate against set reliability, fairness, transparency and explainability metrics; run security tests (manual, automated, cross-validation) by application type: generated-content safeguards; collision and stability for physical devices; explainability, transparency, robustness and backdoor risks for major decisions; protections for minors and special groups. If results fall short, improve (e.g., model tuning) and retest until requirements are met, or redesign.
what_is_tested: Validation metrics; content safety; robustness; backdoor; protections for special groups; retest gate
who_tests: Organisations deploying AI applications; may serve as reference for regulators and third-party testing bodies (Sec. 1)
interpretation_note: TC260 Secretariat practice guide: a standards-related technical document, non-binding. Notes reference GB/T 42888-2023 and GB/T 45654-2025 Sec. 5.2.
language_read: Chinese original read in full (PDF from tc260.org.cn via fetch, text extracted); English paraphrase is unofficial translation

framework: China - TC260-PG-20268A Cybersecurity Standard Practice Guide: AI Application Security Guidelines, General (v1.0-202609, TC260 Secretariat, Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: At deployment, use safety guardrails to identify and block illegal content, prevent prompt injection and runaway execution chains; where third-party protection services are used, test and evaluate their security capability and service continuity; perform security checks on hardware, software and third-party tools, fix known vulnerabilities or mitigate, and track vulnerabilities to prevent supply-chain backdoors.
what_is_tested: Guardrail and third-party security capability; vulnerability checks of deployment components
language_read: Chinese original read in full (PDF from tc260.org.cn via fetch, text extracted); English paraphrase is unofficial translation
